title: Client-profiled admission controller with progressive output morphing
creator: Claire Donovan
description: Problem: During cross-region capacity constraints we frequently see noisy tenants and bursty traffic causing global tail-latency SLO violations. Existing approaches (hard truncation, priority lanes) either drop high-value requests or require heavy operator tuning. Proposal: Implement a client-profiled admission controller that combines lightweight runtime profiling, quota-aware admission, and progressive output morphing (structured truncation, summarization, and partial streaming) as a graceful degradation family. The controller sits in the request gateway and integrates with regional circuit breakers, tenant quotas, and the runtime's KV cache signals. Goal: keep p95/p99 latency within SLO for tiered customers while preserving best-effort utility for lower-tier traffic rather than full rejects.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can classify requests into client profiles (tiered, bursty, best-effort) within 5ms on the gateway path
Admission decisions reduce token generation for accepted degraded requests via morphing policies (truncate, summarize, partial-response) and are reflected in runtime execution path
During a synthetic overload in lab, p95 latency for P1 customers remains <= 400ms and error rate increase for P2 customers is < 5% compared to baseline
Has feature flag gating and rollout plan; can be toggled per-region and per-tenant
End-to-end metrics exposed in console: admission_accept_rate, morphing_applied_rate, observed_quality_regressions per prompt set
Documentation and runbook describing operator actions and rollback steps completed
design_notes: High-level architecture: 1) Gateway probe inserts light-weight classification (client tier + recent success rate + inferred cost estimate). 2) Admission decision engine evaluates policy rules: hard quota check -> precedence lanes -> soft degrade (morph) -> reject. 3) Morphing engine returns an ordered set of degradation transformations: prefix-preserve summarization, token-budgeted truncation with semantic-safety checks, or serving as partial-streamed response with an explicit 'continued' token. 4) Circuit breaker integration: regional CBs expose capacity headroom; controller uses CB state to bias decisions. 5) Cache-aware optimization: if prefix found in KV cache and morphing won't affect cache hits, accept on fast-path. Security: respects tenant isolation and audit logs for all admission decisions.
implementation_steps: Prototype admission engine as a separate microservice behind gateway; add simple policy DSL and unit tests
Implement morphing transforms in runtime layer with feature flags (truncate, summarize, partial-stream API)
Wire gateway -> controller -> runtime path and add propagation of admission metadata to logs and tracing
Add per-tenant profile store (TTL-based) and lightweight estimator for request cost
Integrate with regional circuit breakers and quota service; add metrics and dashboards
End-to-end system tests with synthetic overload across two regions; run canary in us-west-2 for 48h
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal traffic (canary users) - enable in a single non-critical region for 48h
Beta: opt-in tenants (support-assisted) across two regions; collect quality signals and iterate (2 weeks)
Gradual: 10% traffic -> 25% -> 50% per-region with automated rollback on SLO regressions
GA: default on for best-effort tier; P0/P1 customers stay default-accept unless explicitly opted into morphing
test_plan: Unit tests for policy DSL, morphing transforms and semantic-safety checks
Integration test: gateway-controller-runtime path with injected KV cache hits/misses
Chaos test: simulate region partial outage and confirm controller shifts to more aggressive morphing instead of rejecting P1 requests
Quality regression tests: run prompt-set evals to measure ROUGE/embedding-similarity pre/post morphing
Perf test: confirm classification adds <5ms median to gateway path and morphing overhead stays within SLO budget
monitoring_alerts: Alert if morphing_applied_rate increases > 2x baseline and correlating p95_latency climbs > 15%
Alert if admission_reject_rate for P1 customers > 0.5% over 15 minutes
Dashboard panel: per-tenant admission decision breakdown, morph strategy distribution, quality-regression heatmap
SLO check: automated rollback if P95_latency for paying customers > 1.2x target for 10 minutes
